column3: Pairs شريعة with الحكم بما أنزل الله and the prohibition of أهواء; primary parallel.
Sets following الهدى against fear of dispossession and closes with لا يعلمون.
Joins اتباع الهوى to being turned away and falling; direct contrary trajectory.
Commands الاستقامة كما أمرت and rejects أهواء alongside revealed books.
Local opening grounds the surrounding discourse in تنزيل الكتاب من الله.
States that wrongdoers follow أهواءهم بغير علم and contrasts divine guidance.
Forbids following the أهواء of deniers and those who do not believe.
Immediate antecedent: بينات من الأمر, knowledge, and division through بغي.
Uses أتبع سببا as concrete movement by a means, a secondary route pattern.
Combines جعل, الحكم بالحق, and the warning that الهوى diverts from سبيل الله.
Local assertion that the recited آيات are بالحق frames the ensuing imperative.
Contrasts devotion with obeying one whose heart is heedless and who follows هواه.
Supplies a parallel description of الذين لا يعلمون as hearts sealed by God.
Preserves the guidance-versus-clear-deviation contrast as route boundary evidence.
Makes following a marker of affiliation, while disobedience remains distinct.
Rejects أهواء of a people already astray and leading many from السبيل.
بأمره here governs the sea and ships, not the normative route of 45:18.
Contrasts one on بينة from his Lord with those following أهواءهم.
The occurrence of جعل concerns guardianship, without a route or desire relation.
Same-surah expansion: taking الهوى as god, with knowledge and blocked perception.
شُرَّعًا describes the fish; it is a lexical boundary, not شريعة guidance.
Warns against following أهواء after knowledge and names divine guidance as الهدى.
Local continuation places لا يعلمون within the passage's resurrection horizon.
Contrasts following رضوان الله with returning under wrath; only a broad follow pattern.
Links claims made without knowledge to fabricated allocation, indirectly clarifying ignorance.
Separate liability for deeds adds no route, command, or desire relation.
Names those who followed the Prophet, a limited positive affiliation parallel.
Uses شرع لكم من الدين and calls for establishing religion without division.
Local outcome for mockery lacks a distinct link to the imperative in 45:18.
Presents following as pursuit of taught رشد, a positive counterpart to following الهوى.
جعل with another god is not a route or command reading here.
Local cosmic signs do not directly specify شريعة, اتباع, or أهواء.
Parallel phrase اتخذ إلهه هواه; its contrast route is boundary evidence, not support for it.
Following what devils recite is too remote from the stated command and desire contrast.
Makes greater guidance the criterion for what may be followed.
Commands following the messenger and associates it with guidance.
Contrasts unauthorized legislating in الدين with what God has permitted.
Local book-of-record judgment does not add a route reading to 45:18.
Negates speech from الهوى; contrast evidence marks a boundary between speech and inclination.
A claim of receiving favor على علم does not develop the route contrast.
Local creation signs are not a distinct interpretive route for 45:18.
فاتبع قرآنه supplies a narrow obedience pattern without the rival-path contrast.
Uses الأمر for a contested affair; useful boundary against collapsing every أمر into شريعة.
Defines refusal as following أهواء without هدى من الله and calls it utmost misguidance.
يتبعها denotes a consequence after charity, not the directed following at issue.
Asserts that all الأمر belongs to God, a broad authority backdrop only.
Immediate local setting: Israel received الكتاب والحكم والنبوة before 45:17-18.
هاوية preserves a fall image, but only as lexical and secondary trajectory evidence.
يدبر الأمر concerns cosmic governance, delimiting another sense of الأمر.
Physical pursuit by Pharaoh provides no normative following relation.
Commands following what was sent down and rejects other protectors.
Cosmic management of الأمر does not clarify the normative phrase in 45:18.
Local rejection of clear signs contributes only the opponents' immediate setting.
A second أتبع سببا repeats the means-following pattern with little added force.
الأمر is battlefield dispute; this is a boundary reading rather than direct support.
Pharaoh's misguidance lacks the relevant command, following, or desire language.
Following magicians is a contrary allegiance pattern, but not an explanatory parallel.
Pairs steadfastness with not following the way of those who do not know.
Immediate sequel calls the discourse بصائر and هدى for those with certainty.
Limits following to what is revealed, a concise positive counterpart.
Commands following Ibrahim's millah, linking اتباع with a received religious pattern.
Connects arguing without knowledge to following every rebellious devil.
Physical هَوَى retains only a secondary descent image for the contrary reading.
Commands upright orientation toward الدين and rejects association.
Local exhortation to pardon does not clarify the route-command contrast.
يُتبعون concerns attaching harm after charity, a different construction.
Forbids speaking about God without knowledge; it only indirectly frames لا يعلمون.
Names the Qur'an's imposed obligation and distinguishes guidance from clear deviation.
Following is framed as obedience to أمر, but the dialogue gives little further detail.
Combines a divinely made practice, الأمر, and straight guidance.
Local persistence after hearing signs adds no distinct route reading.
Physical casting down is too remote despite the shared descent image.
تتبعها is sequential following, not guidance or desire.
A hostile accusation about whom listeners follow is not explanatory route evidence.
Following divine guidance yields freedom from fear and grief; a broad positive outcome.
What people do not know concerns creation, not the knowledgeable route contrast.
Immediate moral-liability and return frame the then of 45:18.
Disciplined following under a condition is a limited positive model.
Inventing partners بغير علم indirectly parallels claims made without knowledge.
Human honor and provision have no distinct connection to the imperative.
Contrasts following revelation with inherited practice lacking reason or guidance.
Explicitly refuses أهواءكم and identifies their pursuit with being astray.
Local signs for reflection do not add a direct route or desire relation.
States that truth following أهواء would corrupt the heavens and earth.
Reinforces الحكم بما أنزل الله and adds vigilance against diversion from revelation.
The accounting of communities is local context but not a distinct reading of 45:18.
Treats following God's signs as the unfulfilled response before humiliation.
Warns against following أهواء after knowledge, alongside a revealed حكم.
Objections to the truth do not supply a route, command, or desire relation.
Shows souls rejecting what they do not desire; secondary desire-versus-messenger evidence.
Followers and later innovation form a distant, mixed pattern rather than a direct parallel.
Successive messengers and making stories use أتبعنا in an unrelated sequence.
The book made guidance for Israel is a broad local precedent only.
Following the devil marks a contrary allegiance, without the knowledge or law frame.
Sealed hearts and failure to understand lack a route or desire connection.
Following divine guidance explicitly prevents straying and misery.
جعل concerns night and day, unrelated to normative guidance.
A false summons to follow our way exposes a counterfeit route claim.
Text distortion and selective acceptance give only a remote rival-authority setting.
Restraining the self from الهوى is a direct contrary practice to following it.
Directly warns against following أهواءهم after knowledge has come.
Shows the rupture between followers and those followed; secondary allegiance consequence.
Forbids following steps of Satan, a general contrary-route command.
Makes following Ibrahim a marker of rightful affiliation.
Names those who follow الشهوات as seeking a great inclination away.
Contrasts commanded rejection of الطاغوت with seeking its judgment.
After guidance, following other than the believers' way is an explicit rival-route warning.
Links excellence in دين to following the millah of Ibrahim.
Those who follow رضوانه are led through multiple سبل السلام.
Centers judgment on what God sent down, a legal-source parallel to شريعة.
Requires the people of the Gospel to judge by what God sent down therein.
Sets حكم الجاهلية as the contrary to God's judgment.
Limits following to what is revealed; direct positive source boundary.
Declares that الحكم belongs to God alone and that He relates truth.
Majority-led following is tied to misguidance and following ظن.
States that many mislead by أهواءهم بغير علم.
Commands following the straight path and forbids following divergent ways.
Commands following the sent-down book and links it with تقوى.
Defines followers of the messenger through his command and prohibition.
Explicitly joins attachment to earth with اتباع هواه and misguidance.
The messenger states that he follows only what is revealed to him.
Asks whether one who guides to truth is more entitled to be followed.
Most follow only ظن, which does not replace truth.
Treats following alleged partners as following ظن and conjecture.
Forbids leaning toward wrongdoers, a neighboring boundary against rival alignment.
Presents following Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Yaqub as a received millah.
Joins الحكم لله with the command of exclusive worship and الدين القيم.
Names a سبيل grounded in بصيرة, a positive route-and-knowledge parallel.
Forbids inventing halal and haram by speech, directly bounding rival legislation.
The Qur'an guides to what is أقوم, a concise positive route statement.
Forbids pursuing what lacks knowledge; supports the knowledge boundary.
Describes pressure to turn the messenger from what was revealed to him.
Links following الشهوات to the loss signaled by غي.
Commands اتباع and obedience to أمر against the calf's rival pull.
Pairs disputation بغير علم with absence of هدى and كتاب منير.
Addresses the messenger as calling to a صراط مستقيم.
Forbids following steps of Satan; a secondary contrary-route command.
Regrets not taking a سبيل with the messenger, a retrospective route contrast.
Commands upright orientation to الدين حنيفا, a positive directional counterpart.
Contrasts following what God sent down with inherited practice.
Forbids obedience to disbelievers and hypocrites alongside divine awareness.
Commands following what is revealed from the Lord.
Repeats the prohibition of obeying disbelievers and hypocrites.
Records following Iblis except for a believing group, a contrary allegiance pattern.
Commands following those who are guided and seek no payment.
Commends hearing speech and following its best, with divine guidance.
Commands following the best of what was sent down from the Lord.
Invites following a guide to سبيل الرشاد.
Returns disputed matters to God's judgment, an authority boundary.
Links revelation to guidance toward a صراط مستقيم.
Specifies that the straight path is God's path.
Names inherited practice as the path opponents insist on following.
Tests inherited following against a message that is more guiding.
Describes companions who bar from السبيل while assuming guidance.
Contrasts following falsehood with following truth from the Lord.
Links following what angers God with invalidated works.
Explicitly contrasts اتباع الظن وما تهوى الأنفس with guidance from the Lord.
States that those lacking knowledge follow only ظن.
Places the sent-down book in the role of judging disputed matters among people.
Commands following the messenger as the disclosed test of allegiance to God.
Commands following the millah of Ibrahim حنيفا.
Connects holding fast to God with guidance to a straight path.
Orders obedience to God, the messenger, and legitimate authority, with disputes returned to God and the messenger.
Makes acceptance of the messenger's judgment and full submission decisive.
Equates obedience to the messenger with obedience to God.
Contrasts coming to revelation and the messenger with sufficiency in inherited practice.
Commands following the guidance of those whom God has guided.
Commands steadfastness كما أمرت, closely paralleling the commanded direction in 45:18.
The messengers command worship of God and avoidance of الطاغوت, a source-and-rival boundary.
Describes leaders who guide بأمرنا, a secondary positive reading of أمر.
Pairs obedience to God and the messenger with the condition for guidance.
Names worship of God as a straight path.
Commands steadfast orientation toward the one God.
